learningObjective: Precisely define the goal of KV cache quantization in LLM serving.
stem: In LLM inference serving, 'KV cache quantization' primarily targets which resource?

options.text: Reducing the memory footprint of the per-request KV cache (Key and Value tensors stored across decode steps), thereby allowing longer contexts or larger batches on the same GPU memory; and, when the attention kernel reads quantized KVs, reducing attention memory bandwidth.
Reducing the compute cost of attention by using INT8 Tensor Cores for the KV projections.
Reducing the size of the model weights loaded from HBM during decode.
Compressing the input token embeddings before they enter the transformer blocks.

explanation: In LLM inference, the KV cache is the per-request memory that stores K/V projections across all previously generated tokens; it grows linearly with sequence length. For long contexts and large batch sizes, KV cache dominates GPU memory (e.g., a 32K-context 70B model needs tens of GB per request for FP16 KV). Quantizing KV to INT8 or INT4 halves or quarters the footprint, enabling larger batches / longer contexts. If the attention kernel reads KVs at quantized precision, memory bandwidth also drops. Option B: KV compute is a small fraction of total attention work. Option C: model weights are separate. Option D: input embeddings are separate.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: memory footprint and bandwidth of the KV cache.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: KV compute is not the target.

assumptions: Standard Transformer decoder with per-token K/V caches stored across decode steps.
nonImplications: Does not imply KV quantization is free — some accuracy cost is typical.
Does not imply attention kernel automatically supports quantized KVs — kernel-side support is needed.

distractorRationales.B: Confuses KV cache with attention compute.
distractorRationales.C: Confuses KV cache with model weights.
